robots.title: Real-robot task success
robots.caption: 20 trials per task setup and controller. Bimanual success requires completing every subtask.
robots.takeaway: Gated planning improves over BC in all five setups and matches observed always-plan success in four of five.

simulation.title: Simulation benchmarks
simulation.caption: Means across three evaluation seeds. Push-T reports maximum target coverage; Block Pushing and LIBERO report success. Ungated ForesightIL evaluates 32 candidates at every decision. “Subopt.” includes additional suboptimal data.
simulation.takeaway: Comparing predicted outcomes improves over the underlying Diffusion Policy in all four settings.

gate.title: Planning frequency and performance
gate.caption: Mean ± sample SD across three seeds. p is the target planning fraction; “planned” is the measured fraction, including initial context filling. The controlled study keeps the policy, value, and candidate budget fixed within each task.
gate.takeaway: At p = 0.50, evaluation is 1.90× faster on multi-goal Push-T and 1.26× faster on LIBERO than always planning. These wall times include the simulator.

value.title: Learning to rank imagined outcomes
value.caption: Single-goal Push-T maximum coverage, mean ± sample SD across three seeds. All scores use the same policy and world model; N is the number of candidate trajectories.
value.takeaway: VIP with temporal straightening has the highest mean coverage at each candidate budget. Straightening changes the value projection; the policy and dynamics predictor stay fixed.

composition.title: Combining task-specific policies
composition.caption: Mean coverage on Push-T and success rate on Franka BlockPush. The specialist reference averages each policy on its own task; multi-task and fused controllers handle the combined task set.
composition.takeaway: The planner samples from fixed specialists and selects by predicted goal progress. The fused controller outperforms the multi-task baseline in both settings.
